routes.description: Establish that the universe began to exist, defend a causal principle whose metaphysical scope includes that beginning, and show that the resulting explanation can be a transcendent personal efficient cause without preexisting material conditions.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the universe's beginning falls under a defensible metaphysical causal principle, objections based on ordinary material and temporal causation do not establish an exemption, and conceptual analysis supports a transcendent personal cause.

motionBridge.description: Connect the universe's causally explained beginning to a cause beyond spacetime and material reality, with grounds for treating that cause as personal.

centralBridges.description: Establish that being cannot begin from nonbeing and that this principle is not restricted to processes occurring within spacetime.
Establish that the universe can genuinely begin even though no earlier temporal interval exists.
Establish the coherence and explanatory adequacy of efficient causation without a preexisting material cause.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require a relevant basis for exempting the universe from a principle applied to other things that begin.
Explain why allowing an uncaused universe would not license arbitrary substances to begin uncaused.

routes.description: Show that ordinary causal evidence supports principles governing physical processes within spacetime but does not warrant extending efficient causation to the beginning of spacetime and matter or inferring a transcendent personal creator.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the pro side does not justify metaphysical scope beyond observed causal conditions, narrower principles account for ordinary regularity, and the universe's temporal boundary does not independently require transcendent causation.

motionBridge.description: Show that causal regularities within the universe do not supply a warranted bridge to a transcendent cause of the universe.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the evidential basis for causation is bound to spacetime, material conditions, and interaction within physical reality.
Show that induction supporting efficient causes also supports material accompaniment, creating a parity problem for creation without matter.
Distinguish existence at every temporal point from an object appearing after an earlier interval in which it did not exist.
Provide restricted causal principles that preserve ordinary regularity without extending causation to the universe as a whole.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require an account of how causation remains intelligible when no preexisting thing is affected.
Show that a principled exceptional class need not entail arbitrary uncaused objects or unrelated spontaneous events.

sections.title: Physical or Metaphysical Scope of the Causal Principle
sections.rationale: This issue governs whether experience of causation within the universe can justify applying a causal premise to the origin of spacetime and material reality themselves.

sections.title: Material Accompaniment and Immaterial Agent Causation
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether material involvement is essential to intelligible efficient causation and whether personal agency supplies a coherent model of causation without prior matter.

sections.title: Temporal Beginning and the Universe's Boundary
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether existence at every temporal point nevertheless constitutes coming into being and whether ordinary appearance-from-nothing intuitions transfer to the universe.

sections.title: Restricted Causal Principles and Ordinary Regularity
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether narrower causal rules can explain why ordinary objects do not begin uncaused while withholding commitment to an unrestricted metaphysical principle.

sections.title: Selective Uncaused Existence and the Arbitrary-Objects Challenge
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether allowing an uncaused universe makes arbitrary uncaused substances inexplicable, and whether exceptions for particular classes can answer that challenge.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.proposition: If the universe began to exist and everything that begins to exist has a cause, then the universe has a cause whose conceptual analysis supports a beginningless, timeless, spaceless, immaterial, powerful, personal creator.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly yields the floor to Craig, whose uninterrupted opening presentation states and develops the Kalam argument.

response.rationale: This constructive move states the Kalam inference and extends its conclusion through conceptual analysis to a transcendent personal cause.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: As a constructive move, it directly establishes the principal route and its intended motion-level conclusion.

precisionFindings.rationale: The conditional inference and attributed properties are recoverable, though the conceptual-analysis bridge remains compressed.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Craig says the analysis leads, in his view, to the properties, but the excerpt does not supply each derivation.

moves.speaker: Scott Clifton
moves.proposition: Inductive evidence for efficient causes equally supports the principle that whatever has an efficient cause of its existence also has a material cause, so induction alone cannot justify retaining one principle while rejecting the other.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.proposition: Beginning to exist does not require a preceding empty time; it requires that there be no earlier time at which the thing exists, allowing time and the universe to begin without contradiction.
moves.attributionBasis: Craig takes the next uninterrupted turn, directly characterizes Clifton's objection as one about scope, and supplies his alternative definition of beginning.

components.text: The claimed evidential restriction of causal principles to processes within spacetime.
Whether beginning requires an earlier empty temporal interval.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It supplies relevant contrary material and resolves a secondary boundary issue, but leaves the primary scope warrant unanswered.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The definitional proposal supports coherence at the boundary without claiming by itself to prove a cause.

components.text: Whether ordinary causal evidence transfers when its observed background features are removed.

moves.proposition: Material accompaniment may be common rather than essential to efficient causation because an intellectual agent can cause mental events or thoughts that are not constituted from material stuff.

components.text: Whether rejecting a material cause also warrants rejecting an efficient cause of the universe.

moves.proposition: A universe that exists at every temporal point is not aptly described as popping into existence from nothing, so intuitions about objects newly appearing within time do not transfer to the cosmic boundary.

components.text: Whether existence at every temporal point is equivalent to appearing after prior nonexistence.
Whether ordinary popping-into-being intuitions apply to the universe's first boundary.

response.rationale: Clifton directly distinguishes a temporally exhaustive universe from an object appearing within an already existing time.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It explicitly contacts the boundary definition and identifies the decisive difference from ordinary examples.

moves.proposition: On a tensed theory of time the universe genuinely comes into being rather than merely possessing a static front edge, and an uncaused beginning conflicts with the principle that being cannot arise from nonbeing.
moves.attributionBasis: Craig explicitly disagrees with Clifton and sustains the response through the tensed-time analysis, metaphysical principle, Hume discussion, and resulting causal conclusion.

components.text: Whether a first temporal state genuinely comes into being on a tensed theory.
Whether a metaphysical being-from-nonbeing principle reaches the boundary.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The response expressly contacts the decisive temporal interpretation and states the contrary consequence.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response accurately isolates the relevant time-theoretic alternative and does not pretend to refute it unconditionally.

moves.evidenceBasis: Craig contrasts a static front edge with genuine coming into being under tensed time and invokes the principle that being does not arise from nonbeing.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.proposition: The causal principle is metaphysical rather than a scientific law confined to spacetime because it expresses that being cannot arise from nonbeing and that whatever comes into existence requires a cause.
moves.attributionBasis: Craig explicitly answers the scope question in a continuous turn contrasting metaphysical principles with physical laws.

components.text: Whether the causal premise is a metaphysical principle rather than an intracosmic physical law.
Whether missing ordinary physical features defeats the principle's broader application.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It explicitly contacts the decisive scope question and supplies the metaphysical basis for broader application.

moves.evidenceBasis: Craig explicitly calls the principle metaphysical, states that being cannot come from nonbeing, and demands a reason for physical restriction.

moves.speaker: Scott Clifton
moves.proposition: Principles requiring causes only for non-initial things or for things beginning within spacetime can preserve ordinary causal regularity without adopting an unrestricted metaphysical causal principle.
moves.attributionBasis: Following a brief interruption, Clifton gives named and generic alternatives in a clearly attributable continuous turn.

components.text: Whether ordinary regularity requires an unrestricted metaphysical causal principle.
Whether narrower causal rules block arbitrary intracosmic beginnings without reaching the universe.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.proposition: Once an uncaused beginning is allowed for the universe, no stated restriction explains why only universes, rather than bicycles, root beer, or other arbitrary objects, may begin without causes.
moves.attributionBasis: Craig introduces the follow-up explicitly to Clifton and develops the Arthur Prior challenge until Clifton begins his answer.

components.text: Whether the proposed restrictions explain why arbitrary objects cannot begin uncaused.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.proposition: The Kalam causal premise concerns substances that begin to exist and does not commit its defender to the separate proposition that every event has a cause.
moves.attributionBasis: Craig explicitly distinguishes substances from events and explains the argument's neutrality regarding universal event causation.
